mathematical_checks.finding: The Gaussian halves are actual independent product coordinates. The convolution proof uses gaussian_seed_conv with both variances (t+epsilon)/2, obtaining the original sqrt(t+epsilon) factor without assuming covariance invertibility. The seeded law equality is a pushforward/convolution identity, not just a covariance calculation.

The fourth-tensor split is proved with arbitrary jointly measurable B_i(x,a), bounded actual direction copies, and actual Fubini integrability. Its outer xg coordinate remains outside the complete sum over i, so one G0 is shared across all removed-row experiments; the restoration expectation similarly uses one outer Gaussian G1. The mask-to-array identity retains all actual removed-row shifts before this split. This is an equivalent actual experiment route after pushing the original sample/mask data to its retained array, rather than a separately asserted equality of the full original tuple law.

originalSigma is precisely the measurable-space pullback by Prod.fst. conditionalRestorationCoefficient_copy_ae_eq proves actual conditional expectation equality from copyAverage_ae_eq_condExp and Fubini; it supplies measurability and integrability for each finite matrix entry and then combines the entrywise a.e. statements. The independent copy coordinates do not enter the conditioned base coordinate.

The seeded covariance budget is derived by replacing the actual conditional coefficient with the unconditional copy matrix and applying the checked whitened covariance budget. Its conclusion is a quadratic upper bound by normSq, compatible with singular covariance and an ambient support projection. The supporting reconstruction is a.e., transported through actual product projections; no false ambient covariance=identity assertion is introduced.

The shift is exactly r*(1+t)*chosenCopy minus the actual retained row. Its proof combines chosenCopy norm<=delta with the retained-row a.e. bound 2delta, and 0<=r*(1+t)<=2 on the closed unit square, giving 4delta for either copy choice. The shift depends on the same copies as the derivative directions, as permitted by the product bound; no independence of shift from directions is used.

The copied matrix estimate uses only the actual first/base projection, with its pushforward law identified as seededSplitBaseDistribution. Copies are adjoined by product measure. Concentration remains an explicit actual unconditional base-law input; it is not incorrectly asserted after conditioning on a fixed mask or on the entire base sigma-field.

Same-copy fourth moments use restorationCoefficient(mu, whitenedObservation, physicalFace^2), and sign removal is justified by neg_sq. Fresh-copy moments instead use first-copy whitened observations and second-copy physicalFace^2 on mu.prod(mu). relativeFreshFourthMatrix_eq_first_copy factors the latter integral into the two actual second moments, producing the distinct fresh matrix; actual product integrability is proved separately.

Both same and fresh raw relative fourth hypotheses are pulled through the whitening transpose and covariance support projection. The two conditional fourth budget theorems call their respective same/fresh bounds, and seededCopyDirection_conditional_fourth_budget dispatches on Bool without identifying the two matrices. Therefore each remaining slot in all three patterns receives the correct bound.

The repeated direction in the Lean restoration model is always copy factor1. In A, take factor1=printed zeta, with unused factor2; Bool choices are (false,false,false). In B, take factor1=printed tilde_zeta and factor2=printed zeta: (true,true,true) gives [tilde_zeta,tilde_zeta,zeta,zeta] and a zeta shift. In C, the same identification and (false,true,true) give [tilde_zeta,tilde_zeta,tilde_zeta,zeta] and the same zeta shift. Product factors both have law mu, so this is a consistent relabeling of independent copies, equivalently an inner-factor swap preserving the base and common Gaussians. The shift copy is not silently swapped independently of the directions.

Each named original A/B/C path integrand is equated to the actual seeded product expectation through the removed-mask experiment and full retained-array law. A explicitly adjoins an unused fresh coordinate by a measure-preserving projection; B and C unfold directly to the stated Bool branches. Reconstruction of the repeated physical observation from the whitened one is invoked a.e. before the exact Gaussian restoration identity.

The product estimate and each A/B/C bound contain the complete sum over observations inside the expectation and absolute value. The finite tensor envelope proportional to p^4 is used only for Fubini and integrability in the exact identities; the final sharp remainder estimate uses the actual conditional matrix budgets, not the sum of observationwise absolute estimates.

The actual calibrated scalar kernel is uniformly bounded by one on the real unit square. The B/C scalar prefactors and B factor 1-r are separately bounded. abs_unit_intervalIntegral_le_const then bounds each whole signed A/B/C integral; the final triangle inequality is applied to the three complete terms, yielding three copies of the common bound. This matches the printed universal-constant absorption and preserves cancellation across observations.

findings.qualification: The split law theorem itself is a path-law pushforward. The actual fourth-kernel product identities supply the stronger retained-mask/copy/common-Gaussian experiment transport needed here. This review does not claim a separate formal full-tuple joint-law theorem beyond those checked identities.
